title: Circular security with random opening from weaker assumptions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Derive the circular-security-with-random-opening property used in lattice obfuscation from a more conventional circular-security assumption, with an explicit reduction.
status: The 2025 construction introduces a specialized property; ordinary circular encryption security is not an interchangeable assumption.
why: It would clarify whether a proposed simplification of iO assumptions is substantive.
key_works: Hsieh–Jain–Lin (2025), *Lattice-Based Post-Quantum iO from Circular Security with Random Opening Assumption*, ePrint 2025/390.

title: xiO from one-way functions
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Construct exponentially efficient iO from OWFs, achieving output size \(2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,|C|)\) for a constant \(\varepsilon>0\).
status: The 2016 xiO framework isolates nontrivial compression, but an OWF-only construction remains unresolved.
why: Even partial truth-table compression could become a powerful intermediate cryptographic primitive.
key_works: Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, ePrint 2016/006.

title: Polynomial-security xiO-to-iO lifting
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Upgrade polynomially secure xiO to polynomial-time iO without assuming subexponential security for xiO or its auxiliary primitives.
status: The foundational lifting theorem uses subexponential hardness.
why: It would make weak obfuscation constructions much more consequential.
key_works: Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-662-49387-8_17.

title: Decomposable obfuscation directly from plain LWE
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Construct general-purpose decomposable obfuscation directly from ordinary LWE with polynomial security loss.
status: A framework showing what decomposability enables does not itself establish this assumption-specific construction.
why: It could enable useful obfuscation applications before the full plain-LWE iO problem is resolved.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

title: Conjunction obfuscation from ordinary Ring-LWE
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Remove the extra entropic assumption from a useful conjunction-obfuscation construction, or precisely delimit the distributions where ordinary Ring-LWE suffices.
status: The implemented entropic-Ring-LWE route leaves this assumption-reduction question separate.
why: It would strengthen one of the more concrete restricted-obfuscation approaches.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, DOI: 10.1109/SP.2018.00007.

title: Unbounded-collusion public-key FE from plain LWE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct public-key FE for all polynomial-size circuits with arbitrarily many polynomially bounded functional-key queries from ordinary LWE.
status: General FE and bounded-collusion FE exist; the clean-assumption, unrestricted-collusion combination remains unresolved.
why: It would enable expressive encrypted computation without general obfuscation assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, ePrint 2010/543.

title: Unbounded-collusion secret-key FE from OWFs
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct secret-key FE for general circuits from OWFs without fixing the number of issued functional keys at setup.
status: Minimal-assumption bounded-collusion results do not resolve the unbounded regime.
why: It would move a powerful class of selective-decryption capabilities toward minimal assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-642-19571-6_16.

title: General public-key FE from arbitrary PKE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Derive unbounded-collusion general FE from ordinary public-key encryption, allowing non-black-box techniques.
status: Recent decentralized FE obtains bounded-collusion functionality from PKE but uses FE for the unbounded-collusion case.
why: It asks whether ordinary encryption already contains the power of arbitrary selective decryption.
key_works: Goyal–Yadugiri (2025/2026), *Decentralized Multi-Authority Functional Encryption with Malicious Authorities from Standard Assumptions*, ePrint 2025/412.

title: Succinct-encryption general FE from plain LWE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct general FE whose encryption circuit and ciphertext size avoid dependence on a future maximum function size, under ordinary LWE.
status: Succinct encryption is a powerful strengthening: sufficiently secure FE with this property yields iO.
why: Data could be encrypted before the scale of future computations is known.
key_works: Bitansky–Vaikuntanathan (2015/2018), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/163; DOI: 10.1145/3234511.

title: Expressive registered ABE from plain LWE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Obtain expressive registered ABE with malicious registration and compact aggregation from plain LWE alone.
status: Registered constructions using pseudorandom functionalities can inherit additional evasive-assumption dependencies.
why: It would remove master-secret escrow without reintroducing extraordinary assumptions.
key_works: Pal–Schädlich–Tairi (2025), *Registered Functional Encryption for Pseudorandom Functionalities from Lattices*, ePrint 2025/967.

title: Witness encryption from OWFs
subfield: Witness encryption and conditional release
open: Construct NP witness encryption from arbitrary OWFs, allowing non-black-box methods.
status: WE dates to 2013; the general OWF-only standard-model construction remains unresolved.
why: It would greatly lower the foundation required for conditional cryptographic release.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), *Witness Encryption and Its Applications*, DOI: 10.1145/2488608.2488667.

title: A useful trilinear map from established assumptions
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Construct a cryptographically useful trilinear map with efficient operations and a reduction to an independently studied assumption, rather than general iO.
status: The multilinear-form challenge predates candidate graded encodings and remains distinct from their existence.
why: Degree three already enables capabilities unavailable from ordinary pairings.
key_works: Boneh–Silverberg (2003), *Applications of Multilinear Forms to Cryptography*, ePrint 2002/080.

title: Polynomial-arity graded encodings from conventional assumptions
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Support polynomially many multiplicative levels with compact encodings and security based on a conventional assumption.
status: Candidate-map constructions have not become a broadly accepted standard-assumption solution.
why: High arity is the resource required by many ambitious map-based applications.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi (2013), *Candidate Multilinear Maps from Ideal Lattices*, ePrint 2012/610; Gentry–Gorbunov–Halevi (2015), *Graph-Induced Multilinear Maps from Lattices*, ePrint 2014/645.

title: Secure reusable public zero testing
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Provide public zero testing that remains secure under adversarially constructed encodings and repeated correlated tests.
status: Zero-testing interfaces are a central source of attacks on candidate multilinear encodings.
why: The operation that makes encodings useful must not reveal their hidden algebraic structure.
key_works: Cheon–Han–Lee–Ryu–Stehlé (2015), *Cryptanalysis on the Multilinear Map over the Integers and its Related Problems*, ePrint 2014/906.

title: Security of GGH15-style maps beyond zeroizing models
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Prove security of a useful GGH15-style construction against unrestricted efficient attacks, or find attacks outside the protected zeroizing class.
status: “Security against zeroizing attacks” is narrower than full cryptographic security.
why: It would establish whether a surviving candidate family has a defensible security margin.
key_works: Bartusek–Guan–Ma–Zhandry (2018), *Return of GGH15: Provable Security Against Zeroizing Attacks*, ePrint 2018/511.

title: Private DCR-based CPRFs beyond bounded Waring rank
subfield: Constrained pseudorandom functions
open: Extend the DCR construction to substantially broader polynomial predicates without key size growing with a large Waring decomposition.
status: The 2025–2026 construction supports puncturing and bounded-Waring-rank functionality.
why: It would expand useful private constraints without full iO.
key_works: Behera–Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2025/2026), *Privately Constrained PRFs from DCR: Puncturing and Bounded Waring Rank*, ePrint 2025/230.

title: Expressive post-quantum key-homomorphic CPRFs
subfield: Constrained pseudorandom functions
open: Combine key homomorphism with general expressive constraints and full collusion resistance under post-quantum assumptions.
status: Restricted-family key-homomorphic capabilities do not settle the general expressive regime.
why: It would support distributed and proactively refreshed constrained capabilities.
key_works: Langrehr (2025/2026), *Limits on the Power of Constrained PRFs and Identity-based Cryptography*, ePrint 2025/1338.

title: Characterizing copy-protectable function families
subfield: Copy protection and secure software leasing
open: Give structural necessary and sufficient conditions for copy protection of natural function families, rather than seeking protection for every unlearnable family.
status: Conditional impossibility results rule out the latter blanket goal; positive families leave a large classification problem.
why: It would explain what kinds of software can fundamentally be protected.
key_works: Ananth–La Placa (2020/2021), *Secure Software Leasing*, arXiv:2005.05289.

title: One-shot signatures from plain LWE
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Construct one-shot signatures from ordinary LWE without subexponential iO.
status: Standard-model one-shot signatures now exist from stronger assumptions; their existence alone is no longer open.
why: It would give a cleaner foundation for self-consuming authorization capabilities.
key_works: Shmueli–Zhandry (2025/2026), *On One-Shot Signatures, Quantum vs Classical Binding, and Obfuscating Permutations*, ePrint 2025/486.

title: Public quantum money from plain LWE
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Construct reusable publicly verifiable quantum money from ordinary LWE without iO or an idealized group-action model.
status: Generic-model constructions under named assumptions do not establish this standard-model target.
why: It would ground public quantum money in a familiar post-quantum assumption.
key_works: Doliskani (2025/2026), *Public-Key Quantum Money From Standard Assumptions (In The Generic Model)*, ePrint 2025/092.

title: Explicit instantiations of group-action quantum money
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Prove security for explicit group-action families against nongeneric quantum attacks, or exhibit a break.
status: Generic group-action security does not automatically validate a concrete action.
why: This is the direct instantiation problem behind a promising money framework.
key_works: Zhandry (2024), *Quantum Money from Abelian Group Actions*, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2024.101; Doliskani (2025), ePrint 2025/092.

title: Quantum lightning from conventional assumptions
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Construct publicly verifiable quantum lightning under an independently established assumption rather than specialized multicollision or idealized assumptions.
status: Lightning remains stronger than ordinary public quantum money and has its own construction frontier.
why: It would enable publicly recognizable unique quantum resources without a trusted mint.
key_works: Zhandry (2019/2021), *Quantum Lightning Never Strikes the Same State Twice*, arXiv:1711.02276; DOI: 10.1007/s00145-020-09372-x.

title: Unleveled FHE from plain LWE
subfield: Fully homomorphic encryption: construction foundations
open: Construct compact FHE supporting arbitrary polynomial-depth evaluation under fixed setup from ordinary LWE, without circular-security assumptions.
status: Leveled FHE without bootstrapping does not settle this unrestricted-depth target.
why: It would remove a foundational extra assumption from general encrypted computation.
key_works: Brakerski–Gentry–Vaikuntanathan (2012/2014), *(Leveled) Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Bootstrapping*, ePrint 2011/277.

title: Low-overhead protection against approximate-decryption leakage
subfield: FHE rate, native cost, numerical correctness, and implementation
open: Prevent key-recovery leakage from repeated approximate decryptions while preserving useful precision and low overhead under adaptive queries.
status: The security distinction and attacks are established; practical low-cost protection under rich adaptive use remains the target.
why: Numerical error can become a cryptographic side channel.
key_works: Li–Micciancio (2020/2021), *On the Security of Homomorphic Encryption on Approximate Numbers*, ePrint 2020/1533.

title: Adaptive-corruption logarithmic-overhead RAM-MPC
subfield: RAM-model MPC and oblivious memory
open: Extend the three-party logarithmic-overhead RAM-MPC regime to adaptive malicious corruption without idealized erasures.
status: DORAM Revisited establishes a static-corruption malicious baseline.
why: Persistent private services accumulate state that may later be exposed.
key_works: Falk–Noble–Ostrovsky–Shtepel–Zhang (2023), *DORAM Revisited: Maliciously Secure RAM-MPC with Logarithmic Overhead*, ePrint 2023/578.

title: Fully private encrypted-RAM delegation
subfield: RAM-model MPC and oblivious memory
open: Strengthen partially hiding encrypted-RAM delegation so that the desired program and access-pattern information is also hidden, with explicit leakage and succinctness.
status: The 2024–2025 eRAM framework supplies powerful applications but distinguishes partial hiding.
why: Private data owners may also need to conceal the program being executed.
key_works: Afshar–Cheng–Goyal–Yadav–Yadugiri (2024/2025), *Encrypted RAM Delegation*, ePrint 2024/1806.

title: Succinct HSS from polynomial-ratio LWE
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Replace the superpolynomial modulus-to-noise requirement in the relevant succinct HSS construction with a conventional polynomial ratio.
status: Succinct HSS has an LWE route, but its parameter qualification matters.
why: It would improve the assumption and parameter profile of compact distributed computation.
key_works: Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Succinct Homomorphic Secret Sharing*, ePrint 2024/814.

title: Succinct constant-party HSS for general circuits
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Support general circuits with compact shares and output communication under plain LWE, without reducing the problem to large branching-program representations.
status: Succinct HSS for restricted computation models does not settle general-circuit efficiency.
why: It would make distributed encrypted computation expressive without large communication.
key_works: Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Succinct Homomorphic Secret Sharing*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-031-58751-1_11.

title: Post-quantum rate-1 arithmetic garbling
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Match DCR-based rate-1 arithmetic-garbling efficiency under conventional post-quantum assumptions.
status: DCR-based constructions do not provide post-quantum security.
why: Communication-efficient arithmetic MPC needs a quantum-resistant replacement.
key_works: Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Rate-1 Arithmetic Garbling from Homomorphic Secret-Sharing*, ePrint 2024/820.

title: Constant-rate Boolean garbling under plain post-quantum assumptions
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Obtain useful constant-rate garbling measured in Boolean circuit size, rather than amortizing security costs into large arithmetic words.
status: Arithmetic rate-1 results do not automatically imply bit-level rate-1 garbling.
why: Many practical computations are dominated by short-word and Boolean operations.
key_works: Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), ePrint 2024/820.

title: Collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs without stronger algebraic assumptions or an obfuscation helper.
status: Black-box barriers and conditional advances do not settle unrestricted constructions.
why: Collision resistance supports commitments, authentication, and succinct proofs.
key_works: Asharov–Segev (2015), *Limits on the Power of Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/341.

title: Classical oblivious transfer from arbitrary PKE
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Derive classical OT from ordinary PKE without assuming an additional algebraic or completeness property.
status: Black-box incomparability results do not settle unrestricted constructions; allowing quantum communication changes the problem.
why: It asks whether all public-key encryption already enables general private computation.
key_works: Gertner–Kannan–Malkin–Reingold–Viswanathan (2000), *The Relationship between Public Key Encryption and Oblivious Transfer*, DOI: 10.1109/SFCS.2000.892121.

title: Distributional collision resistance from OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct distributional collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs, or strengthen the known separation evidence.
status: This weaker collision notion supports useful primitives not known from OWFs alone.
why: It could bridge part of the gap between inversion hardness and collision resistance.
key_works: Bitansky–Haitner–Komargodski–Yogev (2019), *Distributional Collision Resistance Beyond One-Way Functions*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-17659-4_23.

title: Full-domain post-quantum trapdoor permutations from plain LWE
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct full-domain trapdoor permutations from plain LWE without iO.
status: Full-domain trapdoor permutations from stronger obfuscation assumptions are now constructed; the domain qualification is no longer universally unresolved.
why: It would restore a powerful reversible cryptographic tool under a conventional post-quantum assumption.
key_works: Shmueli–Zhandry (2025/2026), *On One-Shot Signatures, Quantum vs Classical Binding, and Obfuscating Permutations*, ePrint 2025/486.

title: Compact multiparty NIKE from plain post-quantum assumptions
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct noninteractive key exchange for arbitrary polynomial-size groups with one announcement per participant and compact public material from ordinary post-quantum assumptions.
status: iO gives a strong-assumption route; two-party post-quantum NIKE does not settle arbitrary-group NIKE.
why: Mutually distrustful groups could establish shared secrets without interactive coordination.
key_works: Boneh–Zhandry (2014/2017), *Multiparty Key Exchange, Efficient Traitor Tracing, and More from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*, ePrint 2013/642.
